title: cassia cowanii var. peruviana
intro: Cassia cowanii var. peruviana, commonly known as Peruvian Senna, is a plant species in the Fabaceae family, characterized by its bright yellow flowers and pods. Peruvian Senna has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include its ability to treat constipation, diarrhea, and other gastrointestinal issues due to its laxative properties. The therapeutic actions of Peruvian Senna include stimulating bowel movements, reducing inflammation, and exhibiting antimicrobial properties. The bioactive constituents of Peruvian Senna include anthraquinones, which are responsible for its laxative effects, as well as other compounds such as flavonoids and phenolic acids, which contribute to its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities.
